commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[levanter] Load HF safetensors shards concurrently (#9464)

Load indexed Hugging Face safetensors shards concurrently through up to
16 workers. Their range reads share a 16 GiB staging target for each
checkpoint load. Each read reserves twice its byte count until the JAX
transfer completes. Streaming loads also avoid a serial existence
request for every shard.

The 2× reservation is an estimate: expanding dtype conversions can
exceed the target. Loaded model arrays still require their normal device
memory. A matched 32-GPU load time has not been measured yet.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[loom] Archive one-off automation sessions after a minute idle (#9466)

One-off automation profiles (`pr-review`, `agentic-lint`,
`prose-cleanup`,
`fork-ferry`, `codehealth-refinement`) now archive sessions after 60
idle
seconds, and `github-automation` after 30 minutes. `ops` keeps its hour
because its alert coordinators stay alive between alerts.

A session holds its profile's concurrency slot until it is archived.
With
idle timeouts of 15 to 60 minutes, sessions that had already posted
their
results kept slots long enough for later launches to fail with
`profile '<name>' has reached its max_concurrent limit`, even though
each
profile launches only about 6 to 13 sessions a day. `github-automation`
keeps a longer window because it serves user `@weaverbot` mentions,
where
follow-up replies benefit from staying in the same session. Concurrency
limits are unchanged.

The PR-review launcher test is updated for the write-access step added
in
#9457; it failed on main because it expected two workflow steps.

The change takes effect when the `marin-loom` stack is applied.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
Run agentic lint once per PR as a best-effort review (#9463)

The Loom lint review now runs once per PR, only while the PR lacks the
`agentic-lint` label, and is no longer enforced by a required check. The
label records that a lint pass happened, either from the author's local
`./infra/pre-commit.py --review` (the commit skill applies it at PR
creation) or from the Loom session, which adds it after posting
findings.
Pushes to a reviewed PR no longer start another review; removing the
label
requests a fresh review of the current head.

The previous design reviewed every head and gated merging on a per-SHA
completion marker. That posted a new round of comments on every push,
blocked fork PRs and PRs from authors without write access forever, and
left a PR stuck when a Loom run failed, since the per-SHA idempotency
key
prevents a retry. The review is now best effort: a failed run leaves the
label off and does not block merging.

The `agentic-lint` policy job is removed, as is its entry in the
dependency
updater's required checks. The `lint-review` skill no longer names a
Claude-specific inline-comment tool; the Loom agent posts inline
comments
with its own GitHub tools.

Before merging, remove `agentic-lint` from the required status checks in
the "require main CI" ruleset. Otherwise this PR, and every PR after it,
waits on a check that no longer reports.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
Limit agent prose cleanup to trusted authors (#9465)

Prose cleanup now launches only when the issue or PR author has write
access or is `marin-ops-agent[bot]` or `loom-oa-dev[bot]`, using the
same
`check-write-access` action as the other Loom launchers.

Previously the only gate was the `agent-generated` label. A triage user
labeling an external issue or PR would send text written by an untrusted
author to a Loom agent that can edit the description. External issues
and
PRs no longer get prose cleanup.

commits.author: mridulagarwal03
commits.message:
[levanter] Pass pinned tokenizer revisions to Hugging Face (#9450)

Tokenizer staging and `as_hf_tokenizer()` now split a `repo@revision`
ref and pass the revision to `snapshot_download` and
`AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` as a separate argument. Before, the
combined string reached Hugging Face as a repo ID and failed validation,
so a job pinned to a model revision (which `HFCheckpointConverter`
already supports) crashed while staging its tokenizer:

```
HFValidationError: Repo id must use alphanumeric chars, '-', '_' or '.' ... 'openai-community/gpt2@607a30d7...'
```

The split matches `RepoRef.from_string`, which cannot be imported here
without a cycle. Cache and mirror paths keep the full ref, so each
revision stages separately.
`load_tokenizer("openai-community/gpt2@607a30d783dfa663caf39e06633721c8d4cfcd7e")`
and `.as_hf_tokenizer()` now load against the live Hub.

The change and its regression test follow `dfd8a1518f` by @penfever,
which has not landed on `main`.

Fixes #9033

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
Gate Loom launches on live repository permission (#9457)

Loom launch jobs for issue triage, mentions, review autofix, PR review,
and agentic lint now decide eligibility with a shared
`check-write-access` action. It asks GitHub for the event author's
effective repository permission using the workflow token and allows
write, maintain, or admin. A lookup failure logs the API error and
denies the launch. The `marin-ops-agent[bot]` login is passed to the
action's `allowed-bots` input by the two pull-request launchers.

The previous guards compared the event payload's `author_association`
against OWNER, MEMBER, and COLLABORATOR. That payload hides private
organization membership, so every regular member with the default
private visibility resolved to CONTRIBUTOR and was skipped. Over the
last two weeks issue triage ran for four issues, all opened by
organization admins, and never for a regular member. Issue #9192 is one
of the skipped ones.

Local inference startup can now resolve its Gloo network interface on

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
Route GitHub agent workflows through Loom (#9449)

Route GitHub mentions, issue triage, autofix, nightshift jobs, canary
triage, and prose cleanup through workload-federated Loom sessions. Each
Actions workflow launches a named profile from trusted code and passes
run identifiers instead of Claude credentials.

PR #9447 exposed a gap in the existing lint policy: its check required
an `agentic-lint` label, but no workflow ran the lint review, and the
Loom PR review skipped the nightshift bot author. A new PR-head launch
runs the lint catalog review for same-repository maintainer and
nightshift bot PRs, requires a Loom completion marker for the exact head
SHA and refreshes the label only after review. This keeps an old label
from passing a new head. The PR review launcher now admits the
nightshift bot and runs again after head updates.

Canary failure notification remains in Actions while Loom diagnoses from
uploaded artifacts and durable logs. The Iris smoke test continues to
upload screenshots for inspection without launching an LLM review. The
nightshift goals retain their selection rules; the uncalled Claude
runner and cron entrypoints are removed.

After merge, deploy the Loom stack and then the GitHub Pulumi stack. The
policy accepts a local review label for PRs whose base revision predates
the trusted launcher; a base with the launcher requires a completion
marker for the current PR head.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[iris] Route CPU reservations by peer accelerator capacity (#9399)

CPU jobs with `--reserve H100` now prefer an eligible peer with more
effective H100 capacity when other placement scores tie. The marker
requires an H100-capable peer but supplies no numeric GPU gate. In
#9396, five identical CPU reservations all chose `cw-rno2a`; a later
report showed 7 free H100s there and 160 at `cw-us-east-02a`. That
report does not establish the counts at each placement decision.

Among eligible backends with capacity metrics, placement first prefers
no preemption and a tighter fit for any numeric gate. It then compares
capacity for the reserved variant: reported free capacity plus
reclaimable capacity held by lower-priority jobs, less prior
reservations. This affects placement order only. The CPU job charges no
GPUs, later GPU child jobs have no capacity guarantee, and zero reported
capacity does not prevent placement. Peers without a readable capacity
metric rank after measured peers; a peer reporting no capacity for the
variant scores zero.

A stable hash of job and peer IDs now breaks ties before peer ID, so
distinct jobs can choose different peers on one unchanged availability
report. Explicit peer pins and local placement keep their existing
behavior.

Fixes #9396

---------

Co-authored-by: Rafal Wojdyla <ravwojdyla@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Russell Power <607207+rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[iris] Group JAX GPU startup and detect divergent compiles (#9364)

Group Iris's JAX startup code under `iris.jax`: the multi-process GPU
hook and supervisor, compilation and autotune cache setup, distributed
initialization, and compile guard. Levanter, Fray, Grug, and Iris
callers use the new entrypoints. The supervisor launches children before
they import JAX. `initialize_jax()` configures caches before joining the
distributed world and installs the guard after multi-process GPU
initialization.

Before a multi-process GPU compile enters native XLA, the guard compares
JAX compile keys across participating processes. Mismatched keys raise
with each process index and observed key; a missing peer fails after 60
seconds. On `origin/main` at `054142676a`, a two-host H100 probe with a
rank-dependent constant left one rank in
`ConfigAssigner::AssignConfigs`, while the matching control compiled on
both. With the guard, divergent probes failed promptly and matching
probes succeeded on JAX 0.11.0 and 0.11.1. The [issue research
comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9042#issuecomment-5789182658),
[JAX 0.11.0 divergent
run](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fissue-9042-pipeline-divergent-20260922),
and [JAX 0.11.0
control](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fissue-9042-pipeline-control-20260922)
contain the evidence. The 67B Snowball train step was not rerun.

The guard compares JAX's pre-compile key; differences introduced only
inside native XLA remain outside its coverage. Focused Iris, Levanter,
and Fray tests passed (140). The safe affected suite had 5,132 passes, 7
skips, 6 expected failures, and two Tasktrove/Zephyr 30-second timeouts;
both timed-out tests passed in isolation. Repository lint and type
checking passed.

Part of #9042

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
Add Marin Shellbox execution backends (#9433)

Add `marin-shellbox`, a pip-installable execution layer for Harbor
trials and direct machine use. The shared `Machine` API creates a
writable environment from an image source, runs one-shot commands,
transfers files, and owns cleanup.

QEMU and ShellSim have Harbor environment adapters. The Harbor agent
stays in the Harbor process and sends Bash tool calls to a persistent
session. QEMU stages Linux amd64 OCI images from registry references or
Dockerfiles, boots a private microVM, and keeps a PTY-backed Bash
session across agent calls. It probes `/dev/kvm` and falls back to TCG.
ShellSim uses its built-in shell and ignores image instructions.

The machine API also has local Docker and gVisor, Daytona, and Iris
backends. Local gVisor selects a Docker daemon's registered `runsc`
runtime. Daytona creates a sandbox from a registry image. Iris submits a
CPU-only job with its gVisor container profile and uses the existing
exec RPC. Daytona and Iris preserve binary command input and output
through remote files and bound output retrieval. These three backends
currently provide one-shot commands; they need Harbor environment and
persistent shell adapters before `BashAgent` can use them. Iris rejects
network denial because Iris does not expose per-job network policy.

`[qemu]`, `[shellsim]`, `[gvisor]`, `[daytona]`, and `[iris]` select
optional backend dependencies. The gVisor extra does not install or
register `runsc` on the host. The QEMU extra supplies the emulator
through `quicksand-qemu`; a guest kernel, BusyBox, microVM firmware, and
OCI staging tools still need separate provision. QEMU guests have no
network, only Linux amd64 images are supported, and KVM behavior has not
been measured on an eligible host. ShellSim currently shares interpreter
state with verifier actions; its rewards remain exploratory until shell
isolation is available. Task requirements and backend routing are
handled separately from this execution layer.

The shared Python library release builds and checks `marin-shellbox`
alongside the other eight general libraries. They share the daily
development release, the `marin-libs-v*` stable tag, and one version;
Shellbox’s Iris extra pins to that version. Publication uses the
existing OIDC job and the `marin-shellbox` PyPI trusted publisher.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[sft] Connect curriculum generation to Snowball SFT (#9430)

Connect curriculum-generated Datakit conversations to Levanter's
Snowball SFT path and matched evaluations. A preparation step writes
OpenAI `messages` Parquet, and the shared SFT launcher consumes those
artifacts with assistant-only loss and unpacked conversations. The
trainer initializes from
`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.20` at a pinned
revision, runs four updates on 32 H100s, and saves sharded bfloat16
Hugging Face weights. The after evaluation reads the training artifact's
`hf/` directory; there are no separate model import or export jobs.

Generation uses GLM 5.3 beside the relay on cw-us-east-08a and writes
east-region S3 artifacts for training on the RNO2A H100 cluster. Before
and after SFT, the trial uses the same Math500 and
`olympiadbench-deterministic` evaluation settings. The deterministic
benchmark grades symbolic equivalence without an LLM judge, so its
scores are not comparable to the judge-backed OlympiadBench task. The
task is merged in marin-community/evalchemy#178; the runtime lock
records that merge commit from Evalchemy `main`. The branch also retains
a native Grug trainer check that stops on non-finite updates.

A prior native Grug run logged NaN loss at step 2. Its exported
checkpoint scored 0/500 on Math500; the pinned base model scored 306/500
under the same evaluation. The direct Snowball path has not run at full
size, so its accuracy and save time are unmeasured. Generated answers
pass schema, completion, and duplicate checks but are not
oracle-verified. There is no control trained on comparable
non-curriculum tasks; no curriculum effect has been established.

Part of #9193.

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
Fingerprint class-valued config fields by qualified name (#9406)

Class-valued config fields now fingerprint by their qualified name. The
lazy-artifact fingerprint encoder called `np.dtype(o)` on class values
and
expected a `TypeError` for anything that was not a dtype. But
`np.dtype()`
turns any class into the object dtype, so every class encoded as
`{"__dtype__": "object"}`. Swapping one class for another in a config,
such as
a model class, produced no drift warning. `utilities/json_encoder.py`
already
filtered on dtype kind. That filter is now a `scalar_dtype()` helper
shared by
both encoders.

Dead code removed along the way:

- The unused `fake_bundle` parameter of Iris's `InMemoryGcpService`. The
local
and Docker test clusters wrote a placeholder `pyproject.toml` for it on
every
  startup, and nothing ever read it.
- `ShortConvBlockSizes.as_key` in Levanter, which had no callers.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[evals] Bound Evalchemy archive export memory (#9130)

Stream lm-eval JSONL normalization one record at a time and retain only
compact per-document grading summaries while computing coverage. A
completed MMLU-Pro evaluation produced a 2.84 GB sample file and
exhausted the 16 GiB orchestrator during archive export; a 34.2 MB
regression fixture now peaks at 68.5 MB of traced Python memory instead
of 105.9 MB.

Numeric Evalchemy identity fields such as `sample_ordinal` and
`source_id` no longer become sample metrics. Scoreless custom tasks may
use an aggregate item count as coverage evidence only when it is
integral and exactly matches the attempted extent; `n_correct` remains
unknown without item-level verdicts. Extraction filters remain part of
the archive merge key even when a row has no grade, so rebuilding
preserved sources supersedes the intended row without manufacturing a
score.

The affected archive, measurement, and evaluation suites pass 94 tests.
The changed-file gate passes lint, formatting, type checking, and
repository checks.

commits.message:
Allow unpadded expert stacks to retain Muon sharding (#9278)

Allow Muon updates to retain expert sharding when the matrix stack needs
no padding. Stacks that need padding still require a replicated target
axis.

The regression runs with two emulated CPU devices in a subprocess,
including from a single-device CI lane. It compares the update with the
unsharded Newton–Schulz path and checks that the result retains expert
sharding.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[snowball] Expose June model stages for pipeline execution (#8978)

Expose the June Snowball transformer through Levanter and split it into
contiguous pipeline stages that retain the original attention schedule.
Each stage owns and loads only its HF tensor subset, including the
embedding or output boundary when appropriate. Explicit position IDs,
causal segment masks, configurable expert capacity, and routing-drop
counters support packed expert-parallel execution.

Keep the demonstrated RMS, embedding-gather, and router-sigmoid rounding
boundaries. Model tests cover HF loading, masked values and gradients,
uneven stage partitions, and exact parameter ownership. These model
changes are independent of the GRPO objective, pipeline scheduler, and
checkpoint lifecycle; the full migration also needs its scorer-only
compute-cast correction. Numerical evidence and its scope are recorded
in https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/363.

The original two-file model suite passed 31/31 on one CoreWeave H100 in
Iris job `/dlwh/pr8978-h100-20260924-retry8`. The worker preflight ran
Torch and JAX GPU operations on that H100; deterministic XLA GPU
operations keep the exact scoring and differentiated-forward comparisons
reproducible.

planning and text materialization

shingles, then by the document-ID hash modulo 16

document ID
- records source-shard lineage and split parameters; rejects missing
candidate text and inconsistent text for repeated IDs
